Title: #NSTviral: Redang coral reefs deteriorating amid overtourism, poor awareness [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Coral reefs around Pulau Redang are showing signs of continued deterioration, with increasing tourist activity, anchoring practices and low awareness among some visitors placing added pressure on the island's marine ecosystem.
The concerns were highlighted in a recent Instagram video by content creator and mobilegraphy enthusiast @N.muif, which featured data collected by a team working with Reef Check, an organisation dedicated to protecting and conserving marine ecosystems.
The data, collected after the Covid-19 pandemic in 2021, indicated that the condition of coral reefs around Redang had continued to decline year by year.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Najmuddin Muif Bin Zulkifli (@n.muif)
"After Covid-19 in 2021, when we started collecting data, we could clearly see that the coral reefs in Redang were deteriorating year by year," the video said.
The video attributed much of the pressure to overtourism, with large numbers of visitors concentrating at the same snorkelling sites.
"Most of it is caused by overtourism. Too many people are going to just one snorkelling site. Coral reefs cannot withstand overcrowding because they come under stress," it said.
Another concern highlighted was a shortage of mooring buoys, which could result in boats dropping anchors directly onto the seabed.
The video said this could damage coral reefs, including areas undergoing restoration.
"There are not enough buoys, so boats have to find their own way by dropping anchors into the sea. At times, coral reefs that we have planted as part of restoration programmes are damaged by anchors."
The video also highlighted concerns over awareness among some tourists and day-trip operators about marine conservation, including visitors stepping on coral reefs and taking marine life.
"Due to a lack of awareness, some people step on coral reefs and take sea cucumbers. They do not realise that these actions are wrong."
The growing number of visitors was also linked to increasing amounts of solid waste on the island, adding further pressure to its environment.
"As tourist numbers increase, the amount of rubbish on the island also increases. But Redang can still be saved. We need to start now," it said.
The video has since drawn attention online, with several users calling for stronger enforcement and greater awareness among tourism operators and visitors.
One user, Aishawong, said the state government should take action and provide training for day-trip operators to improve their knowledge of marine conservation.
"Redang is very beautiful. The last time I went, the corals were all beautiful," she wrote.
Another user, Tera Ibrahim, suggested tighter rules for boat operators and guides, including selecting operators who demonstrate greater awareness and requiring them to sign agreements with the Redang Marine Park authorities.
"Fine them if they break the rules," the user added.
Farah Hanafi, meanwhile, praised the video for raising awareness in a calm and respectful manner.
"Sometimes, awareness doesn't have to be loud. This is calm, meaningful and powerful," she wrote, thanking the creator for producing the awareness video without resorting to abusive or offensive language.

Title: OGA 2026 brings oil, gas and energy players under one roof
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Oil & Gas Asia (OGA) 2026 returns to provide a platform for players in the oil and gas industry — including policymakers, energy companies, engineering firms and investors — to connect and collaborate.
Held under the theme "Powering Progress, Shaping Tomorrow", the 22nd edition of OGA will be held at Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre from Sept 2 to Sept 4, organised by Informa Markets Malaysia.
"Southeast Asia's energy sector is entering a pivotal period of growth and transformation. Meeting the region's future energy needs will require closer collaboration across the entire value chain — from policymakers and producers to technology providers, investors and innovators," said Informa Markets country general manager Gerard Leeuwenburgh.
"OGA has long been where these connections are forged, bringing together the people, technologies and expertise that turn industry conversations into partnerships, investments and long-term business opportunities," he added.
OGA will welcome Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) back as corporate partner for the fifth consecutive edition.
"Petronas works alongside partners across the value chain to deliver energy safely, reliably and sustainably while advancing energy transition. Our integrated portfolio, from upstream to new energy, gives us the reach to support energy security and lower-carbon solutions in parallel, not as competing priorities," said a Petronas representative.
"We invite visitors to the Petronas booth at Hall 1 to meet our team, explore licensing opportunities, and discuss how partnership and technology translate into value across the ecosystem."
Reflecting the importance of collaboration and market access to Malaysia's oil, gas and services equipment (OGSE) sector, Malaysia Petroleum Resources Corporation (MPRC) highlighted OGA's role in supporting the industry's regional ambitions.
"OGA brings together key energy industry players under one roof, creating meaningful opportunities for collaboration, innovation and business growth.
"As the national OGSE development partner, MPRC is proud to be part of the journey as Malaysia's OGSE companies take their place on the regional stage," said MPRC president and chief executive officer Mohd Yazid Ja'afar.
Despite volatile market conditions, OGA's continued growth reinforces the vital role of B2B platforms in connecting businesses to new markets.
Country pavilions from Australia, China, Germany, India, Italy, Singapore, South Korea and the United Kingdom will showcase technologies, engineering expertise and solutions spanning upstream, midstream and downstream operations, as well as digitalisation and emerging energy technologies.
Beyond the exhibition, a comprehensive knowledge programme — anchored by SPEAK OGA, EIC Connect OGA and MOGSEC — will connect policy, leadership, technology and commercial opportunity.
SPEAK OGA, the event's flagship free-to-attend knowledge-sharing platform, will bring together industry experts and decision-makers together to explore the trends, technologies and priorities shaping the future of energy.
Organised in partnership with the Energy Industries Council (EIC), EIC Connect OGA will offer a global business perspective through market intelligence, project insights and emerging opportunities, while creating connections between companies and key decision-makers across the international energy supply chain.
Registration for the event is now open and industry professionals are encouraged to secure their participation and join the conversations shaping the region's energy future. For more information and to register, visit www.oilandgas-asia.com

Title: Muzz, Coffee Meets Bagel step up safeguards as romance scams evolve
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dating platforms are stepping up verification, moderation and user-safety measures to combat scammers who exploit online relationships to build trust before targeting victims for money and personal information.
Muslim dating and marriage application Muzz has made selfie verification compulsory for new members joining the platform, as part of measures to detect fake profiles and prevent banned users from returning.
Muzz Asia-Pacific Region Growth lead Ary Mozta said the platform used automated and manual checks to ensure users were genuine and that their profile photos matched their verification selfies.
"We also use additional signals such as location, device, email, phone number as well as proprietary fingerprint information to identify inconsistencies.
"We have measures to detect previously banned individuals attempting to return to the platform through new accounts, although due to limitations of the Apple and Google platforms this is not foolproof," he told the New Straits Times.
Ary said users could also voluntarily undergo identity verification by submitting their passport or government-issued identification, with those who completed the process receiving a blue badge on their profiles.
"Beyond verification, Muzz has a 24/7 community team helping users deal with bad actors and any issue they have on our platform," he said.
"We take pride in having an all-female community team providing support, because we believe in providing a safe space for our members at all times."
Ary said Muzz also sought to reduce opportunities for fraudulent behaviour by keeping communication within the app, with members able to make voice and video calls without sharing their personal phone numbers.
The platform also offered photo privacy features and allowed users to add a chaperone, or wali, of their choosing to conversations, he said.
"These features are important because scams can involve building trust over time before a financial request is made.
"We regularly remind our members that they should never send money, share financial information or participate in investment opportunities recommended by someone they met on Muzz," he said.
He said users were encouraged to report suspicious behaviour immediately, with the platform also displaying a warning when it detected that a phone number had been shared.
Ary said that identity verification alone did not guarantee that a user was trustworthy or could not subsequently attempt to scam another person.
Meanwhile, Coffee Meets Bagel (CMB) Trust & Safety head Rachel Tee said the platform used multiple layers of protection to detect and prevent romance scams, fake investment schemes and other forms of fraud.
These included selfie verification, automated systems designed to identify suspicious behaviour, message moderation, human review, and in-app reporting and blocking tools.
"We take reports of suspected fraudulent, abusive or exploitative behaviour seriously," she said.
Tee said CMB's Trust & Safety team reviewed reports alongside behavioural signals, account history and available evidence before taking enforcement action, including banning the account.
The team aimed to review reports within 24 hours, with serious violations potentially resulting in an account being removed from the platform, she said.
Tee said the platform also used information from individual reports and emerging scam patterns to strengthen its detection systems and policies.
"No single safeguard can eliminate online scams entirely, so our approach is to combine technology, verification, human oversight, user education and cooperation with law enforcement to make it increasingly difficult for bad actors to operate on CMB."
She said CMB was prepared to cooperate with the authorities when it received valid requests through the appropriate channels and in accordance with laws and privacy requirements.
"Where users believes they have been the victim of a scam, we encourage them to report the incident to the authorities, as they are best placed to provide first-hand details of what happened, supporting evidence and any information required as part of an investigation.
"Our role is to support that process.
"This may include preserving platform information, explaining what information may be available from us, and cooperating with authorities when we receive a request through the appropriate channels.
"This approach allows users to report their experiences directly while enabling us to support any resulting investigation in a lawful, accurate and privacy-conscious manner," she said.

Title: No mandatory dating app ID checks as govt targets romance scams
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: There are no plans to introduce mandatory identity verification for dating app users, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching. Instead, she said the government was focusing on stronger platform safeguards, improved scam detection and greater public awareness to tackle online fraud.
While identity verification could help reduce fraudulent accounts, she noted it was not a complete solution, as scammers continued to exploit stolen identities, compromised accounts, mule accounts and sophisticated social engineering tactics. "Effective protection requires complementary safeguards implemented across the digital ecosystem," she told the New Straits Times.
These included detection and removal of fraudulent accounts, impersonation attempts and coordinated scam networks; behavioural and technical measures to identify suspicious activities; accessible reporting mechanisms; timely enforcement action and preservation of information to support investigations.
Yesterday, the NST reported that in the past four years up to June, 462 Malaysians — more than 70 per cent of them aged between 21 and 40—lost a combined RM32.7 million to scams originating from people they met on dating platforms.
That works out to an average of almost RM20,000 disappearing every day between January 2022 and June this year.
[[nid:1517420]]
Rather than asking victims for money outright, syndicates are using dating platforms to build trust before steering victims to cross-platform crimes, including fake investment schemes, bogus trading platforms and cryptocurrency scams — leaving victims with devastating financial losses.
Teo said the government continually reviewed online safety risks and international regulatory developments to determine whether additional safeguards were necessary for Malaysia.
This included assessing measures adopted in other jurisdictions, such as identity verification, age assurance, account integrity measures and broader platform safety requirements, while considering their effectiveness, proportionality, privacy implications and compatibility with Malaysia's legal framework.
"There is no decision to introduce mandatory identity verification for users of dating applications," she said.
Teo said romance scams should not be viewed as a problem limited to dating apps, as many cases began on social media platforms or messaging services before progressing to private communication channels.
"So romance scams are increasingly a cross-platform crime rather than one associated with a single online service.
"The government adopts a layered and risk-based approach to combating online scams, recognising that no single measure can eliminate this threat."
Teo said online service providers played an important role in strengthening trust and safety measures, including detecting and removing fraudulent accounts, impersonation attempts and coordinated scam networks.
Platforms should also deploy behavioural and technical measures to identify suspicious activities, provide accessible reporting and complaint mechanisms, take timely enforcement action against accounts used for scam activities, and preserve relevant information to support investigations, she said.
The government would continue disrupting the scam ecosystem through action involving communications channels, online services and digital infrastructure exploited by criminal syndicates, Teo said.
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, she added, would continue working with telecommunications service providers and online platforms to reduce opportunities for scammers to misuse digital services and communication networks.
Financial institutions also played a critical role by strengthening fraud detection capabilities, identifying suspicious transactions, intervening before funds were transferred and supporting rapid financial intervention through the National Scam Response Centre.
Teo said these efforts were complemented by public awareness initiatives, including the Kempen Internet Selamat, to educate people about recognising scam tactics and reporting suspicious activities promptly.
"Ultimately, protecting users online is a shared responsibility.
"Effective protection depends on stronger platform safeguards, coordinated enforcement, rapid financial intervention and informed users who remain vigilant against scam tactics," she said.

Title: Perkeso battles evolving fraud [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of company executives and doctors facing  court action over false Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) claims highlights  the growing  complexity of fraud cases handled  by the government agency.
While  cases have declined overall, Perkeso is seeing a worrying trend involving suspicious claims linked to government  assistance programmes.
These initiatives include PenjanaKerjaya, the Wage Subsidy Programme and Daya Kerjaya.
"Those involved are continually adapting their methods and looking for new ways to circumvent  controls," said Perkeso group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed.
"In some cases, these activities appear to be carried out systematically by people or groups who treat fraud as a source of income," he told the
New Straits Times.
"Based on the cases detected over the past three years, Perkeso's main concern is not simply the number of suspicious claims, but their increasing complexity and potential financial impact."
HOW FRAUD IS CARRIED OUT
Azman said some employers and company owners  set up shell companies, registered people who were not actually employed, or "ghost workers", and falsified monthly payroll records to obtain government hiring grants.
"In other cases, a small number of corrupt doctors from public or private clinics    colluded with syndicates to falsify clinical charts, backdate medical documents or exaggerate disabilities.
"Then you have runners who act as middlemen and recruit vulnerable people, such as the unemployed, the disabled or senior citizens.
"They collect their identity cards, manage the forged paperwork and later  split the illegal  payouts with the recruits."
Azman said some  sophisticated fraud syndicates operated through networks involving  employers, doctors and runners.
He said one of Perkeso's main challenges was that syndicates were  making  false claims harder to detect by preparing  convincing documents, coordinating with  multiple parties providing misleading information.
"Such arrangements make it more difficult to detect irregularities through document reviews alone."
[[nid:1517438]]
Azman said some employers working  with syndicates might also provide inaccurate employment records, contribution histories, wages, attendance records, details of accidents or information about a  claimant's actual employment status.
"However, the involvement of an employer, medical practitioner or agent in a claim does not in itself indicate wrongdoing.
"Each  case must be assessed objectively and investigated based on the available evidence."
HOW PERKESO DETECTS FRAUD CASES
Azman said claims that triggered fraud-detection filters or other red flags would be referred to the Anti-Fraud, Ethics and Integrity Division for further investigation, with the process taking  several weeks to eight months.
The time taken depends  on the complexity of the fraud, as probes can involve verifying information with  clinics, conducting interviews and carrying out field investigations.
He said common red flags included employers offering members of the public small one-off payments of up to RM200 to "borrow" their MyKad.
"Another red flag is a sudden and unusually large increase in employee registrations by a small, inactive or dormant business.
"There are also commuting accident claims or supporting medical records originating from clinics located an unusually long
distance from the claimant's registered home address or principal place of employment.
"For example, a claimant living and working in Kuala Lumpur may submit documents issued in Johor Baru. These indicators do not necessarily prove that fraud has occurred, but may warrant additional verification or investigation."
ADDRESSING RISKS OF COMPLEX FRAUD CASES
Azman said Perkeso wanted greater digital integration in the healthcare system.
"Ideally, medical reports and other relevant records should be transmitted directly and securely by authorised hospitals and clinics, thereby reducing reliance on documents submitted by claimants or intermediaries."
He said more information-sharing among healthcare providers, government agencies and other relevant institutions through a secure and standardised platform would also enable more effective verification.
"This would help minimise opportunities for document manipulation, strengthen fraud detection and protect the integrity of the social security system."
In the longer term, stronger legal provisions and appropriately severe penalties should be considered to deter fraudulent claims, he said.
Azman said the law should address not only claimants who knowingly submitted false claims, but also agents, medical practitioners, touts and other parties who facilitated, organised or benefited from such activities.
He said Perkeso's monitoring was not limited to new applications and that it  was also reviewing previously approved and paid claims.
PERKESO'S SUCCESS SO FAR
Azman said Perkeso was working  with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission  through specialised crackdowns such as Op Hire 1.0 and 2.0, Op Ilat and Op Stroke.
These operations have seen more than 1,600 companies flagged, resulting in  RM61 million being prevented from being wrongfully paid out, while another RM3.8 million has been recovered from employers who admitted to false declarations.
"More than 100 people, including company directors, corrupt agents and panel doctors, have been arrested and  charged in connection with the cases."

Title: 'Sirens shouldn't override traffic rules,' say experts [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The rules governing the use of sirens and beacon lights by emergency vehicles and VIP escorts need a  review to ensure traffic priority does not compromise public safety, experts said.
They said there should be clear, uniform criteria on when sirens and beacons can be activated, who can authorise their use and under what circumstances.
Such privileges should be treated as an operational necessity, not an automatic entitlement based on rank or status.
Escort movements, they said, must also be made safer and more predictable for other road users, with standard procedures covering speed, lane changes, overtaking and intersections, while giving motorists enough time to react.
Universiti Putra Malaysia Road Safety Research Centre head Associate Professor Dr Law Teik Hua said the review should examine how escort movements were conducted, as the main hazard was not the sirens or escort vehicles themselves, but how priority movements were carried out.
[[nid:1517428]]
"This is especially dangerous at intersections, where  ordinary   drivers might not realise where the escort car is coming from or whether there are other vehicles that have been stopped," he said.
Law said while sirens and beacons could indicate that emergency and escort vehicles had priority, drivers still had to follow standard road safety practices.
He said a dedicated standard operating procedure would be the most effective way to improve VIP and emergency movements.
The procedure, he said, should specify when sirens and beacons could be used, permissible speed limits, procedures for lane changes and overtaking, and mandatory speed reductions at intersections and crossings.
[[nid:1517427]]
Meanwhile, senior criminologist Datuk Dr P. Sundramoorthy proposed a three-tier framework covering security, operational necessity and ceremonial or protocol movements, with traffic priority normally limited to the first two when objectively justified.
"Rank alone should not create an automatic entitlement," he said, adding that protection did not necessarily require sirens and flashing lights on every journey.
He said the law already regulated the fitting and use of special warning lights, with authorised categories specified.
"The Road Transport Department (RTD), for example, states that police, Fire and Rescue Department, ambulance and RTD vehicles are among those permitted to use such equipment, subject to  rules.
"However, there is an important distinction between being authorised to possess or use an emergency warning device and being justified in activating it for a particular journey," he said.
[[nid:1517426]]
Road Safety Council member and social activist Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye echoed the call for a full review of the rules.
He said the concerns were justified, as VIP escorts and certain emergency vehicles often moved on the roads in ways that put other drivers at  risk.
Drivers, he said, usually have to brake hard, swerve into crowded lanes, or slow down suddenly, often with barely enough time to react safely.
"It is even more worrying when sirens and beacon lights are treated not as urgent warnings, but as a free pass.
"Some drivers seem to think that with a siren, speed limits do not matter and red lights need not be obeyed.
"They expect every other road user to get out of the way instantly, without thinking about road conditions or other people's safety.
"These are safety tools, not symbols of status," he said.
Lee said that while most agree that the prime minister, royalty and official foreign guests deserved such escorts, their use should be an exception rather than a right for ministers and senior officials.
"No one is above the law. A siren does not cancel traffic rules, and a flashing light does not make safety less important.
"Every road user, no matter their rank, deserves to travel safely, and every road user must drive with care."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israel warns Hamas over kite launches from Gaza
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israel warned Hamas on Sunday that it would step up operations in Gaza if launches of kites, drones and balloons towards Israel continued, after a recent increase in such incidents, while Hamas denied responsibility.
Israeli media reported that four kites were found in communities near the Gaza border on Saturday and one was shot down by the army on Sunday, bringing the total number recovered in recent days to around 10.
The incidents have revived memories of waves of incendiary kites and balloons launched from Gaza in previous years, which sparked fires in agricultural lands in southern Israel.
According to the reports, the Israeli military believes Hamas was behind the launches, which did not carry explosives, and may have been testing how Israel would respond.
"Israel warns Hamas that if the launches towards Israel do not cease immediately, the IDF will take action to intensify targeted operations against those responsible... and will evacuate the population from areas from which kites, drones and balloons are launched," Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz said in a joint statement.
They said they had held a security assessment with top military and security officials on Sunday to discuss the matter.
Uri Epstein, a leader for Gaza border communities – many of which were attacked by Hamas on Oct 7, 2023 – told Channel 12 that "after Oct 7, we will no longer tolerate the words 'It will be ok'."
"The writing is in the sky, and it's the army's responsibility to act in time."
Hamas meanwhile denied responsibility for the launches.
Bassem Naim, a member of Hamas's political bureau, said in a statement that the kites were "launched from Gaza by children searching for their innocent childhood amid the rubble."
In a separate statement, the group accused Israel of using the kites as a "pretext" for airstrikes in central Gaza on Sunday, in which three people were killed according to Gaza's civil defence rescue service.

Title: Norwegian King Harald's health has 'deteriorated', palace says
Article:
OSLO: The health of Norway's 89-year-old King Harald V, who is in hospital due to complications from a blood condition, has "deteriorated" over the weekend, a statement from the palace said on Sunday.
Europe's oldest reigning monarch is being treated for haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells which leads to fatigue, paleness and shortness of breath.
"His Majesty the King's health deteriorated over the weekend," said the palace.
"The King is receiving antibiotics for a bacterial infection in his blood and has responded to this treatment," the statement added.
He was admitted to Oslo University Hospital on Monday due to fluid retention from the cortisone treatment he is receiving and placed on sick leave for two weeks.
The palace has previously said the King had cancelled his visit to the central region of Trondelag scheduled for Sept 1 and 2, after the end of the previously announced sick leave period.
Several members of his family have visited him in hospital.
The Verdens Gang newspaper reported that his wife, Queen Sonja, their son Crown Prince Haakon, who is acting as regent in Harald's absence, and Haakon's wife Crown Princess Mette-Marit visited him on Sunday, as did the King's sister.
None of them made a statement upon leaving the hospital.
TURBULENT YEARS
Harald, who ascended the Norwegian throne in 1991, has had multiple health problems in recent years, forcing him to have a pacemaker fitted and to scale back his official schedule.
But he has always ruled out abdicating, arguing that he took a lifelong oath before the Norwegian Parliament.
In February, he was hospitalised for an infection and dehydration in Tenerife, where he was on a private trip with Queen Sonja.
His wife, also 89, was briefly admitted to hospital in May due to heart problems.
Harald's health woes come at a turbulent time for the Norwegian royal family. Haakon's wife Mette-Marit is under scrutiny for her ties to the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Documents published in January in the United States revealed her sustained and at times intimate correspondence with Epstein between 2011 and 2014, at a time when the American financier had already been convicted.
Mette-Marit's son from a previous marriage, Marius Borg Hoiby, is also in the spotlight as a result of his legal troubles.
He was sentenced in June to four years in prison for two rapes and 32 other charges, including violence against a former partner. He has appealed the verdict.
Suffering herself from a serious lung disease, Mette-Marit, 53, also had to undergo a lung transplant in July.
The royals remain broadly popular with the Norwegian public, in large part due to Harald's unifying figure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Landslide at Guinea landfill kills 30
Article:
CONAKRY: A landslide at a landfill in Guinea's capital killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted the collapse of a massive mound of waste that engulfed nearby tents and shacks.
The incident occurred less than a week after the government announced plans to close the site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the ongoing rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa.
The landslide took place at around 2am (0200 GMT) in the Gbessia commune of Conakry, according to a government statement. The death toll was 30, with six people seriously injured and 16 more lightly injured, the statement said.
Rescue workers were using excavators and other tools to clear the site of the landslide, which witnesses said was large enough to bury an apartment building along with more precarious dwellings.
One woman, Cire Diallo, told reporters at the scene that her five children were killed.
"I have lost all my children. All I can do is put my trust in God," she said.
Guinea holds the world's largest bauxite reserves and richest untapped iron ore deposit at Simandou, where a massive mining project was launched in November.
But the West African country has poor infrastructure and widespread poverty, with 3.7 million of its 15.1 million people living on less than US$4.20 per day, according to a World Bank report published in April.
Guinea's Minister of Territorial Administration, Djenab Toure, announced on Thursday that the government was closing the landfill because it was unsafe and said the waste was to be relocated outside Conakry.
Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah visited the landfill on Sunday to assess the damage and supervise the response, the government statement said, adding that people should "remain calm, show solidarity, and strictly follow the instructions of rescue services and the competent authorities."

Title: Trump takes starring role at Washington's IndyCar debut
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump rode a ceremonial lap in his armoured limousine and waved the green flag to start Sunday's IndyCar race through the streets of Washington, capping celebrations of America's 250th birthday.
Trump, who created the Freedom 250 Grand Prix by executive order for the United States anniversary commemoration, had a prime view of the spectacle as open-wheel cars roared past iconic landmarks at speeds of up to 185 mph (298 km/h).
"It has turned out to be bigger than we ever thought possible," Trump told race telecaster Fox. "The track is wonderful. I want everyone to be safe and the people to have a good time."
American Kyle Kirkwood won his seventh career IndyCar race, his sixth on a street course, beating Denmark's Christian Lundgaard by 3.09 seconds, with Australian Will Power third and Sweden's Marcus Ericsson fourth.
"You can't even put it into words. This is incredible," Kirkwood said. "I'm almost in tears. This is a big moment for us. A big moment for America."
Trump greeted IndyCar series owner Roger Penske, 89, and the seven Indianapolis 500 winners in the field of 25 before the 147-lap event began, telling the racers, "Good luck, do well, have fun."
"Roger told me they had been trying to do it for 20 years and when Trump came along they got it done," the 80-year-old president said.
[[nid:1517385]]
'BIG FAN'
Trump and First Lady Melania Trump were inside his armoured limousine known as "The Beast" as the vehicle and his motorcade slowly took a lap around the 1.7-mile layout, which weaved around such landmarks as the Washington Monument, US Capitol, National Archives and museums such as the National Gallery of Art.
"The president wanted to do this. He's a big fan. We wanted to be part of the 250th anniversary," Penske said.
"This is really a by-product of our team trying to take it to the next level. This is an iconic race."
Flyovers were next, including ones by a stealth bomber and Air Force One, and air traffic was paused at nearby Reagan National Airport due to the race.
Trump then waved the green flag at the start-finish line in front of the US Capitol building to begin the 250-mile race.
"The 100,000 people who will be coming here today, they care about the country," Penske said. "They are excited to see us racing here."
Trump has taken major roles in other events to celebrate the anniversary of the July 4, 1776, signing of the Declaration of Independence – housed inside the course at the National Archives – marking the split of 13 original American colonies from Britain.
Among the activities was an Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) bout in a huge cage on the White House lawn in June.
New Zealand's Scott McLaughlin crashed into a tyre barrier on a restart with 19 laps remaining while trying to pass leader Kirkwood, who sped away on the next restart with 13 laps to go and led to the finish, spinning his tyres at the finish line after a victory lap.
"It was a hard race," Kirkwood said. "It felt good to dominate out there. I don't know if we're ever going to have another chance, I hope we do, but this was awesome. A dream come true."
[[nid:1517384]]
'IT'S A SPECTACLE'
Spanish pole-sitter Alex Palou, a six-time winner this year, was overtaken by Kirkwood and had a penalty, poor tyre change and crash on his way to finishing 20th, dooming his bid to clinch a fourth consecutive season title in Washington.
IndyCar and Penske Racing are paying much of the US$35 million cost to stage the race, supported by sponsors of a series best known for the Indianapolis 500 oval classic.
Mario Andretti, the 86-year-old US racing legend whose 1969 Indy 500-winning car is in the Smithsonian, was impressed.
"Fabulous to be here. This event is really amazing," Andretti said. "Can't be any better than this."
It figures to be a once-in-a-lifetime extravaganza.
"I don't know if we'll ever drive IndyCars around the nation's capital again, so the fact we're doing it is a spectacle," US racer Josef Newgarden said. "This feels like the Indy 500."
Penske said IndyCar would consider returning.
"Never say no. We'll talk about it," Penske said. "We'll have to meet next week and figure out where we're going next."
US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum likes the idea, saying, "This is a really positive thing. Everybody I've met is saying 'Please do this again next year.'"
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tens of thousands ordered to evacuate in Nevada as fire threatens Reno
Article:
NEW YORK: Tens of thousands of people have been evacuated this weekend from the area of Reno, Nevada, and many others were under orders to leave on Sunday as a wildfire reached the outskirts of the state's third-most populous city.
About 42,000 residents have been displaced or are in active evacuation areas, with an additional 45,000 under a "be prepared to evacuate" status as the Hawk Fire threatened northern Reno, local officials said late Sunday morning.
Local TV footage showed flames approaching roads. In eyewitness video verified by Reuters, smoke from the hills billowed over nearby residential neighbourhoods.
Fire-tracking websites showed evacuation zones extending from the Sierra Nevada hills to the University of Nevada in northwest Reno.
The fire has burned 13,000 acres (5,261 hectares) so far, officials said at a press conference on Sunday. The fire was human-caused and remains under investigation, they said.
Three civilians and three first responders have been injured, said Shane Akerson, a commander leading fire and rescue operations.
Officials first received reports of a fire off Hawk Meadow Trail at about 11.15am PDT (1815 GMT) on Saturday, said Richard Edwards, chief of Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District. Firefighters on Saturday worked amid "extreme red flag conditions", he said.
Red flag conditions are a combination of warm temperatures, very low humidity and strong winds that raise the risk of wildfires.
"We expect those same strong conditions to come back this afternoon," Edwards said on Sunday.
Nevada Governor Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency late Saturday in Washoe County, which includes Reno and parts of Lake Tahoe.
"This is an active and rapidly evolving situation, and I urge everyone in the affected areas to remain vigilant and follow the direction of local officials," Lombardo said in a statement.
Lombardo authorised the deployment of two National Guard helicopters to help fight fires and 60 National Guard personnel to support operations with the Washoe County Sheriff's Office, officials said.
The Reno-Tahoe International Airport remained outside the evacuation area, and commercial flights were operating normally on Sunday.

Title: [UPDATED] Syria, Israel hold US-mediated talks to ease tensions
Article:
DAMASCUS: Syria and Israel held high-level, US-mediated talks in Jordan on Sunday aimed at easing tensions following recent Israeli strikes on Syrian territory, Syria's state news agency SANA reported, citing a diplomatic source at the foreign ministry.
The talks focused on practical mechanisms to halt Israeli strikes, arrests and targeted operations, and on reviving negotiations towards a security agreement that could lay the groundwork for a broader future accord, SANA said.
The two sides also discussed efforts to ease tensions between Israel and Turkey and to prevent their rivalry from spilling onto Syrian territory.
Syria's Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani told Reuters on Saturday that Damascus expected security negotiations with Israel to resume soon, although he added that there was a lack of trust between them.
Talks had been suspended since the start of the Iran war, while Syria cut off contact entirely after Israeli strikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase last week, according to Shaibani.
Washington has for more than a year sought to broker a security agreement between Israel and the government of Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.
Shaibani said the two sides had agreed on paper to "almost everything" around the beginning of the year, including arrangements for security zones in southern Syria and a buffer zone where only United Nations forces would be present, but Damascus doubted Israel's willingness to implement the agreement.
The Israeli prime minister's office did not reply to a request for comment on Shaibani's remarks.
At Sunday's meeting, SANA said, Syria indicated that its immediate priorities remained an Israeli withdrawal to positions held before Bashar al-Assad's overthrow on Dec 8, 2024, and the full restoration of a 1974 disengagement agreement.
Damascus also told the Israeli delegation it would not accept arrangements restricting its right to rebuild and develop its armed forces or determine its alliances and partnerships, SANA said.
Syria reiterated that the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights were Syrian territory but said discussions over the region's final status were premature, according to the SANA report.
Israel has carried out repeated strikes on Syrian military sites since Assad's fall, saying its actions were necessary to protect its security. Syria has denied posing a threat to Israel and has demanded an end to Israeli strikes and incursions.
Syria and Israel have technically been at war since 1948. Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the 1967 Six-Day War and later annexed it, a move recognised by the United States but not by most of the international community.

Title: Selangor, Putrajaya step up flood fight
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
PUTRAJAYA: The Selangor and federal governments have agreed on five measures to reduce flooding in the Klang Valley.
In a joint statement following a meeting between Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, both sides agreed to hold a technical meeting within two weeks.
"Other measures include assessing the capacity of Batu Dam and Klang Gate Dam, identifying sites for new flood retention ponds, upgrading three ponds and coordinating river dredging and desilting works," the statement said.
The technical meeting will determine project locations, scope, estimated costs, funding sources and implementation methods, with preliminary details to be prepared before the next parliamentary sitting and the tabling of the 2027 Budget.
Regular meetings will also be held to monitor progress and resolve outstanding issues.
Both sides agreed to study whether Batu Dam and Klang Gate Dam have sufficient capacity to meet water management needs over the next 20 to 30 years.
They will also identify suitable upstream locations for new flood retention ponds.
The assessment will consider technical suitability, land status, environmental and community impacts, and each site's ability to reduce flood risks.
The Selangor Irrigation and Drainage Department will identify three existing ponds for upgrading: Kampung Laksamana Pond, Sungai Kertas Pond and Bukit Lagong Pond.
Bukit Lagong Pond is located in a forest reserve and  would need to be degazetted before it could be used as a flood retention pond.
The Selangor and Kuala Lumpur Irrigation and Drainage Departments will identify rivers requiring dredging and desilting.
The Kuala Lumpur Irrigation and Drainage Department will also help identify a suitable 12ha site in Selangor for the disposal of dredged material.—Bernama

Title: Quake near Tokyo injures 37, disrupts train services
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
TOKYO: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck near Tokyo early yesterday, injuring at least 37 people and disrupting travel in the megacity.
The quake caused violent shaking in the Japanese capital and its surrounding areas, prompting warning systems to sound public announcements and sirens in the streets and lighting up smartphones with notices in affected areas.
The quake struck the southern part of the Ibaraki Prefecture near Tokyo at 2am, the Japan Meteorological Agency said.
There were no concerns about a tsunami, the agency said, adding that the earthquake's depth was 68km.
The US Geological Survey estimated the strength at magnitude 5.8.
Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency said at least 37 people had suffered minor injuries.
The late-night quake disrupted regional train services in the capital city yesterday morning, according to East Japan Railway Company.
A building in Saitama, north of Tokyo, also suffered minor damage, according to the Fire and Disaster Management Agency.
Authorities were investigating if a water main that ruptured in a neighbourhood in the capital was related to the quake, Kyodo News said.
The weather agency warned of an increased risk of landslides in the area as the quake could have loosened soil in the region, which was lashed by torrential downpours on Saturday.
The agency also warned of the possibility of strong aftershocks in the days ahead.—AFP

Title: 1,000 youths light up Kota Baru
Article:

KOTA BARU: Nearly 1,000 youths, including 20 disabled people, took part in a 3km walk here on Saturday night to celebrate patriotism and unity ahead of National Day.
The inaugural Madani Glow Walk brought together youths from various backgrounds, including tertiary students, to mark the celebrations.
Kelantan Youth Joint Council information chief Ezzat Hanuzi said the event aimed to foster community spirit and nurture patriotism through a simple yet meaningful activity.
Participants carried glow sticks and waved the Jalur Gemilang, creating a sea of light in the city centre.

The walk began at the Kota Baru Cultural Centre towards the city centre.
Ezzat said the walk served as a platform for youths to show their love for the country.
"We want to show that young people understand the meaning of independence. Walking together with lights and flags creates a lively atmosphere and proves that the patriotic spirit remains strong."
He said having deaf and mute participants showed that patriotism transcended age, background and physical ability.

Title: Rubber market  to trade higher on strong demand
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian rubber market is expected to trade higher this  week, supported by strong demand and concerns over supply constraints.
The Malaysian Rubber Glove Manufacturers Association (Margma) said demand is expected to strengthen, particularly in China, which has pledged additional fiscal policy measures aimed at supporting economic growth.
"Demand for premium and sustainably sourced natural rubber is also expected to strengthen as Malaysian glove manufacturers place greater emphasis on traceability and sustainability under the European Union Deforestation Regulation  requirements."
In addition, Margma said El Nino concerns could potentially disrupt rubber production and constrain supply across rubber-producing countries.
Industry expert Denis Low said the Malaysian rubber market is expected to trend slightly higher next week, supported by potential restocking demand from China and firmer crude oil prices.
"Reports of sizeable dry rubber replenishment in China could provide  upward momentum if buying volumes are substantial, while higher oil prices may also lend support to natural rubber prices.
"Supply and demand remain relatively balanced, although foreign exchange volatility and adverse weather in major producing regions could influence prices."
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the Malaysian Rubber Board's reference price for Standard Malaysian Rubber 20 added 38 sen to 947.0 sen per kilogramme, while latex in bulk decreased nine sen to 679.5 sen per kilogramme.—Bernama

Title: China tax crackdown forcing wealthy investors to assess offshore trusts
Article:
A growing campaign to tax offshore wealth is forcing wealthy Chinese people to rethink their trust structures and investment holdings, lawyers and advisers say, as Beijing sharpens its focus on capital outflows and rule enforcement amid growing fiscal strains.
In late July, authorities overhauled rules to impose a 20 per cent income tax on offshore trusts, while tax offices in major cities like Beijing and Hangzhou have started to enforce taxation on returns from offshore insurance policies.
Those measures have triggered a scramble among some wealthy individuals to assess their liabilities, raise cash to meet them and revamp investment holdings.
At stake is a collection of capital worth up to US$1.2 trillion held by mainland Chinese ultra-high-net-worth individuals, according to a report from consulting group BCG earlier this year, parked in Hong Kong, Singapore and other low-tax jurisdictions.
More than half of China's super-rich individuals use offshore family trusts to manage their wealth, reports from KPMG showed.
Offshore trusts have gained popularity in recent years as a growing number of Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong. This unlocked billions of dollars for their founders.
Before the introduction of the new rules in late July governing the taxation of offshore trusts, such structures operated in a regulatory grey area without a standardised and dedicated regime.
The new rules apply a tax of 20 per cent on the appreciation in value at the time of a transfer of shares, property or other assets into offshore trusts. Income from such trusts and offshore entities that they control will also be taxed annually at 20 per cent.
Unpaid taxes on assets placed in trusts since January 2023 and on trust income received before 2026 must be reported within 90 days.
"For those preparing for a listing, they are considering unwinding trusts," said Shanghai-based Luo, who provides cross-border tax advice to clients.
A Hong Kong-based executive at a state brokerage said some clients were avoiding setting up trusts and investing through smaller offshore asset managers instead.
Some may be forced to dispose of assets to meet obligations.
"Based on my discussions with Chinese lawyers, it looks like if they have a trust and they are Chinese citizens, they have to declare," said Singapore-based Ryan Lin, a lawyer who advises high-net-worth clients.
Out of the more than 50 trust clients that Lin advises, over half are prepared to declare assets and pay taxes, while the remainder are considering unwinding their trusts.
"Many are considering liquidating mainland A-shares to raise cash amid recent market volatility."
An executive at a Chinese tech billionaire's family office in Hong Kong said some wealthy individuals may need to borrow money to pay their tax bills because much of their wealth is tied up in illiquid assets like real estate.
For many wealthy Chinese, however, the larger concern is not their immediate tax bill, but what might come next.
Soon after unveiling the imposition of taxes on assets in offshore trusts, Chinese authorities began levying taxes on insurance policy income earned offshore, media reports said.
The new measures "signal broader tax reforms as authorities seek diversified revenue sources", said Carlos Casanova, senior economist for Asia at UBP, a Swiss private bank, as China's real estate downturn weighs on provincial governments' ability to generate revenue from land sales.
A Shanghai-based family office partner said some clients feared scrutiny beyond tax compliance, especially by being subjected to a probe into how they got money out of China in the first place.
The tax push is also supported by Beijing's expanding data-gathering capabilities.The Common Reporting Standard, implemented in 2017, gave Chinese authorities greater visibility into offshore financial accounts.
Combined with the Golden Tax Phase Four system, they can cross-check information across multiple jurisdictions.
"The enforcement campaign is unprecedented and appears here to stay," said Christopher Beddor, deputy China research director at Gavekal Dragonomics, adding that most investors likely never paid tax on offshore income due to lax rule enforcement.
"It's easy to imagine how this could merge into other goals, such as tougher enforcement of capital controls."
The writers are from Reuters

Title: Energy crisis just getting started
Article:
The Iran war has pushed the global oil refining industry to the brink, signalling that diesel and petrol prices may remain elevated for years.
Deal or no deal, the global energy inflation shock is far from over.
While oil markets adapted remarkably well to the abrupt loss of a fifth of global crude supplies from the Middle East during the conflict, workarounds for the refining industry have been far more limited.
The divergence between crude and fuel prices tells the story.
Benchmark Brent crude oil is currently around US$90 a barrel.
Even though that is up about 25 per cent from levels at the outbreak of the conflict on Feb 28, it is a significant retreat from the wartime peak at US$118.
Refined products have not enjoyed the same relief. European diesel prices have surged more than 70 per cent since the war began, while petrol prices in the United States have climbed around 60 per cent.
This reflects a dramatic decline in refining output.
The war knocked out more than 20 per cent of the Middle East's 9.6 million barrels per day (bpd) of refining capacity, according to the International Energy Agency, while fuel exports remain suppressed due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
The loss of Gulf crude led many refiners, particularly in Asia, to curtail operations. That strain was then amplified by months of relentless Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.
These attacks have cut Russia's refining throughput by 30 per cent to below four million bpd in recent months, forcing Moscow to ban diesel exports in July.
Meanwhile, diesel refining margins in Europe, Asia and the US have surged to unprecedented levels.
European diesel cracks have more than tripled since February to above US$75 a barrel. US diesel margins have climbed more than 140 per cent, reaching a record US$100 earlier last week.
The crisis has been mitigated somewhat by pre-war fuel stockpiles — but that buffer is essentially gone.
Global oil stocks fell at a rate of 3.5 million bpd between March and July, equivalent to more than three per cent of global oil demand, and are expected to continue declining until year-end.
Sky-high prices also reduced demand among businesses and consumers, but not by enough to fully offset the supply crunch.
Demand for refined products last quarter fell by four million bpd, leaving more than one million bpd shortfall.
The balance is expected to deteriorate further in the third quarter. Refinery runs are projected to be 4.1 million bpd lower year-on-year, while demand is expected to decline by just 2.4 million bpd.
The direction is clear: fuel supply is shrinking faster than demand.
What if a diplomatic breakthrough between Washington and Teheran permanently reopens the Strait of Hormuz?
While that would likely lead to a plunge in crude prices, it probably would not deliver quick relief in the refined product market because more than 20 refineries across the Gulf suffered damage during the war.
China's response to the tightening supplies will also be critical.
The world's second-largest refiner sharply reduced its processing rates and curtailed fuel exports during the war.
Demand destruction could prove more significant than currently projected as consumers and businesses pull back on spending in the face of eye-watering energy bills.
But the urgent need to replenish global fuel inventories should add upward pressure to refining demand, potentially for years.
Many Wall Street analysts and economists still assume the energy price spike will be a short-term phenomenon unlikely to feed through to core inflation.
But if the refined product crisis is as serious as current data suggests, that assumption may be too optimistic. This is especially true in Europe and Asia, where liquefied natural gas prices have also spiked.
The US has not been immune to rising energy prices, and the risk to current projections through year end is clearly tilted to the upside.
Nearly six months into the Iran war, the world appears to be witnessing a slow-motion crash.
The fuel market's safety buffer has been stripped away as inventories have been depleted, while disruptions caused by the war continue to strain the overstressed refining system.
The energy crisis that really matters to the global economy is just getting started.
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'We have faced this many times': Pas ready for action over Hadi's article

Title: MSF condemns Israel's closure of probes into attacks killing 4 staff
Article:
GENEVA: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has condemned the Israeli authorities' decision to close two cases referred by the organisation for review without opening criminal investigations, the Palestine News and Info Agency (WAFA) reported.
The two cases concern multiple attacks on an MSF convoy in Gaza City in November 2023, which killed two people, and an airstrike on an MSF shelter in Khan Younis in February 2024, which killed two people and injured six others.
In a statement, MSF said the decision came nearly two years after it submitted its requests and after the organisation petitioned the Israeli Supreme Court over the military prosecutor's failure to respond to its formal requests.
MSF described the decision as unjust and unacceptable, criticising the closure of the cases after two years of silence.
This is not surprising when a military institution is tasked with investigating its own actions," the organisation said, arguing that the system had demonstrated an unwillingness to address violations in Gaza that may amount to war crimes.
MSF said its staff members and their family members had been killed by Israeli forces despite the organisation having notified Israeli authorities of their locations. The vehicles involved were also clearly marked with the organisation's emblem, it said.
The organisation said the decision effectively confirmed that there would be no meaningful accountability within Israel's legal system for the deaths of its staff, and called for the cases to be reviewed by an independent, impartial investigative body.
According to MSF, 15 of its staff members have been killed by Israeli forces in Gaza since October 2023, along with around 1,700 healthcare workers.
MSF reiterated that no military objective can justify the mass killing of civilians and that an internal military review cannot replace genuine, independent and impartial accountability.
– Bernama-WAFA

Title: One of two men nabbed by Thai cops also on Kelantan police's wanted list
Article:

He said one of the suspects, in his 30s, was on the police's wanted list.

two Malaysians were arrested

Title: Over RM720 mil spent on welfare aid for seniors, PwD, chronic patients - Nancy
Article:
KUCHING: The Social Welfare Department has spent about RM728.5 million to support the welfare of senior citizens, persons with disabilities (PwD) and chronic patients nationwide as of June this year.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the allocation was channelled through the Senior Citizen Assistance (BWE) and the Assistance for Care of Bedridden Persons with Disabilities and Bedridden Chronic Patients (BPT).
"To ease the burden on families, the Social Welfare Department also assists with the care of bedridden persons with disabilities, bedridden chronic patients and non-bedridden chronic patients who meet the eligibility criteria.
"As of June 2026, a total of 42,036 recipients nationwide had received this assistance, involving expenditure of more than RM119.5 million," she said when officiating the Sarawak-level SPeKTRUM Caregiver Support Programme at the state branch of Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka (DBP) here today.
Nancy said during the same period, BWE was channelled to 170,133 recipients nationwide, involving expenditure of more than RM609 million.
On the distribution in Sarawak, she said 23,034 senior citizens in the state had benefited from BWE, involving an allocation of more than RM94.3 million, while more than RM10.4 million had been channelled to 3,235 BPT recipients in the state.
Meanwhile, Nancy said that strengthening the country's care ecosystem was important, particularly to ensure the welfare of caregivers looking after these groups was also safeguarded.
She said the responsibility of caring for those who were frail or bedridden should not rest solely on families without strong support from various quarters.
"That is why, through SPeKTRUM, caregivers are provided with training, psychosocial support and motivation so that they can provide the best care without neglecting their own health," she said.

Title: Bersatu leaders accuse Pas of pre-empting ROS on supreme council quorum issue
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu leaders today accused Pas, which leads Perikatan Nasional (PN), of pre-empting the Registrar of Societies (ROS) over claims that Bersatu no longer has the quorum to hold meetings of its Supreme Leadership Council.
Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said that, to date, ROS itself had never issued any statement questioning Bersatu's legitimacy or announced that the party had been dissolved.
"This is the problem with Pas' power-hungry attitude to the extent they even want to do ROS' job. What does the PN seat negotiations committee meeting for the Negri Sembilan state election have to do with the claim that the supreme council meeting did not have a quorum?
"Where in the Bersatu Constitution does it state that Bersatu loses its legitimacy and is dissolved merely because there is an allegation that its supreme council meeting does not have a sufficient quorum?" he said in a statement on his Facebook page today.
He was commenting on media reports quoting Pas leaders, including PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, as saying that PN had decided not to invite Bersatu to attend its coalition meetings after the party was alleged to have only 23 supreme council members, falling short of the 25-member quorum stipulated in its constitution.
Takiyuddin said the matter was raised after four Bersatu MPs lodged a complaint with ROS on July 13 over claims that the party had lost the quorum to hold supreme council meetings.
Tun Faisal said the matter of quorum was clearly provided for under the Bersatu Constitution, with Clause 13.12 stating that the quorum for a supreme council meeting was half of the total number of council members.
"The constitution does not state that the figure must be based on the original number of supreme council members after the party election, as Pas is attempting to interpret it.
"The provision merely uses the phrase 'total number of supreme council members'. Therefore, if the number of members currently holding office is 20, the required quorum is 10. This is what happens when one does not understand the difference between the words 'membership' and 'total number of members'," he said.
Meanwhile, former private secretary to Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, Datuk Marzuki Mohamad, said the PN secretary-general had no authority to issue a show-cause letter to Bersatu over the complaint lodged by Bersatu MPs with ROS regarding the quorum for its supreme council meetings.
He said the PN secretary-general should seek clarification from ROS, rather than Bersatu, as only the agency had the authority to determine whether an organisation was legally valid.
"Bersatu has, to date, not received any notice from ROS regarding the issue of the supreme council quorum.
"Therefore, at the time the PN Supreme Council meeting was held on July 16, 2026, and up to now, Bersatu remains a legitimate organisation and a legitimate member of PN. This was also acknowledged by the PN chairman in his statement to the media on Aug 9, 2026," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Communities celebrate National Month through arts, cultural heritage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The spirit of the National Month is expressed not only by flying the Jalur Gemilang but also through appreciation of cultural heritage and creative arts among the community.
The community's participation in various events organised in their neighbourhoods also provides parents with a platform to instil patriotism in their children in a more relaxed, creative and enjoyable setting.
For Normaizan Mohd Salleh, 45, her participation in a decorative arrangement competition, in which she created a
tanjak
(traditional Malay headgear), hibiscus and
keris
using fabric, headscarves and prayer mats, was not only an effort to promote cultural heritage but also an opportunity to introduce the spirit of independence to her four children.
She said her participation in the event also gave her children an opportunity to see first-hand efforts to promote cultural heritage in the spirit of the National Day celebrations.
"This is my way of celebrating independence, while also giving my children an opportunity to learn about and familiarise themselves with our cultural heritage and symbols associated with independence," she told Bernama.
Normaizan, who won first place in the decorative arrangement competition, spoke to Bernama at the Jiwa Merdeka Indera Mahkota programme organised by Pertubuhan Wanita Anggun Inspirasi Kuantan (WANGI) here today.
Normaizan said her participation in the programme also encouraged her third child, Asfa Nur Nelydhia Hasmisham, 11, to take part in the independence-themed traditional attire competition.
"My daughter wore traditional attire combining Malay and Chinese elements as a symbol of cultural diversity and harmony among the country's multiracial society, and she won third place today," she said.
Nur Syamimi Abdul Razak, 33, said she encouraged her daughter, Nur Nabilah Sumayyah Mohd Hassan Hafiz, 11, to participate in the independence-themed traditional attire competition to expose her to the role of the young generations as custodians of the country's cultural heritage and identity.
She said the participation of young people, particularly Gen Z, in cultural and independence-themed activities could help them discover the uniqueness of local heritage while fostering pride in their national identity.
"My daughter wore a Puteri Perak outfit showcasing the traditional elements and unique culture of the state. Through participation in activities like this, she can learn about traditional attire and appreciate our heritage," she said, adding that Nur Nabilah emerged champion in her category.
Meanwhile, WANGI chairperson Farahida Fauzi said apart from promoting cultural heritage, the programme also served as a platform to foster unity among the multi-racial members of the local community.
She said the activities organised included traditional games, colouring competitions, e-sports, and a Merdeka quiz.
"This is our initiative to strengthen ties and bring the community closer so that we can embrace the spirit of independence together and appreciate the cultural diversity that forms the country's identity.
"Through the Jiwa Merdeka programme, we also want to convey the message that independence gives us freedom in various aspects, including freedom of expression, the freedom to live comfortably and to interact with one another regardless of race or background," she said.
